events.extended_summary: The European Commission has proposed a €45bn loan for Ukraine in 2027 to address a looming cash crisis and reinforce defenses amid continued Russian attacks. The plan allocates €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian needs such as schools and hospitals. Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed confidence all 27 member states would back the loan, despite Slovakia, Czechia, Hungary and Bulgaria opting out. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who identified a €70bn funding gap for 2027, urged swift adoption, saying strong support signals to Russia that the war must end. The EU aims to cover €45bn while other allies cover the rest, with Ukraine repaying only after Russia pays for damages. This follows a €90bn loan agreed 11 months ago, though escalating attacks have raised costs. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz warned he would block the EU's seven-year budget unless all countries participate.
events.micro_summary: The EU proposes a €45bn loan for Ukraine in 2027 to fund defense and civilian needs amid ongoing Russian attacks.
events.summary: The European Commission proposes a €45bn loan for Ukraine in 2027, split between €25bn for weapons and €20bn for civilian services, to address a €70bn funding gap and strengthen Kyiv's position in peace talks.

events.extended_summary: Anthropic's stock begins trading later this week in an initial public offering that prices shares between $70 and $78, giving the company behind the Claude AI chatbot a total value exceeding $1 trillion. This valuation would make Anthropic one of Wall Street's biggest stocks, rivaling Walmart and JPMorgan Chase, and surpassing the combined value of Coca-Cola, IBM, Starbucks, Delta Air Lines and General Motors. The company could join the Nasdaq 100 index within weeks, which would trigger automatic purchases by funds like Invesco's QQQ ETF holding roughly $457 billion. Entry into the S&P 500 would take longer, requiring at least 12 months of trading. As a public benefit corporation, Anthropic will balance stockholder interests with its goal of responsible development of advanced AI, giving investors less control than typical public companies.
events.micro_summary: Anthropic begins trading with a valuation exceeding $1 trillion after pricing shares between $70 and $78.
events.summary: Anthropic's initial public offering begins trading this week, with shares priced between $70 and $78, valuing the AI company at over $1 trillion and making it one of Wall Street's largest stocks.

events.extended_summary: Ukraine's strike campaign against Russian refineries has knocked out about 55% of capacity, hitting at least 13 plants and reducing total oil processing to an estimated 3.7 million barrels per day, roughly a third below prewar levels. The Ryazan refinery has lost about 90% of capacity while the Omsk refinery lost half. In response, authorities authorized production of lower-grade gasoline below K5 or Euro-5 standards, permitting fuel as low as Euro-2 until July 2027. Deputy Prime Minister Alexander Novak instructed officials to prioritize petrol imports and secure out-of-class fuel. Russia imported over 416,000 metric tons of petrol products by sea in August and another 234,000 metric tons in September, surging from a previous monthly maximum of 5,000 metric tons. Gasoline rationing has been announced in at least six regions, capping customers at 30 liters per day.
events.micro_summary: Ukraine's refinery strikes have forced Russia to import record fuel volumes and produce lower-grade gasoline domestically.
events.summary: Ukraine's strikes on Russian refineries have knocked out about 55% of capacity, forcing Moscow to import over 416,000 metric tons of fuel in August and authorize production of lower-grade gasoline below Euro-5 standards to avert shortages.

events.extended_summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen airport, the first time he has done so with any visiting leader since becoming president, reciprocating Trump's gesture at Joint Base Andrews in September. The two leaders hugged and exchanged words before joining Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit venue for handshakes and a banquet. Xi pledged to stand against trade protectionism while urging support for free and open trade, and Putin criticized Western sanctions imposed over Russia's invasion of Ukraine. The three leaders are scheduled to meet on the sidelines for a one-hour trilateral discussion covering the Ukraine and Iran wars, trade, artificial intelligence and nuclear weapons. Trump will also hold a separate one-on-one meeting with Putin. The gathering has drawn comparisons to the 1945 Yalta Conference.
events.micro_summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in Shenzhen.
events.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping greeted US President Donald Trump at Shenzhen airport ahead of a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit, where the three leaders will discuss Ukraine, trade and nuclear weapons.

events.extended_summary: President Donald Trump, 80, arrived at Malacañang Palace in Manila on Wednesday for a luncheon with Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. before traveling to China for a summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. During a red-carpet greeting, Trump appeared to fail recognizing his own Cabinet members and White House staff, including Chief of Staff Steven Miller, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, and Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who laughed as he shook their hands. Inside the palace, Trump referenced Gen. Douglas MacArthur and asked why he should not receive a gold baton and field marshal rank, and ranted about Christmas decorations. He later met 97-year-old former first lady Imelda Marcos, telling her 'we love you.' During the red carpet walk, Trump veered from a straight path and stopped frequently, and he has also been seen repeatedly tapping his thigh while walking in Washington.
events.micro_summary: President Trump, 80, appeared to forget his own Cabinet members during a Manila visit with President Marcos Jr.
events.summary: President Donald Trump, 80, arrived at Malacañang Palace in Manila for a luncheon with President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., where he appeared to fail recognizing his own Cabinet members while his aides laughed, before departing for a China summit.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces launched a surprise multi-pronged attack on Tuesday, destroying the central road section of the Kerch bridge connecting occupied Crimea with Russia. The operation involved hundreds of attack drones launched from central Ukraine at 10pm on Monday evening, flying approximately 500km over land and the Black Sea over four hours to reach the target. A Dutch-headquartered company stated its missiles were the only foreign-made weapons used in the strike. Following the attack, the Russian Embassy in the Netherlands posted a statement on Wednesday asking whether the Netherlands had openly joined the conflict, referencing the company's admission. The bridge, opened by President Vladimir Putin in 2018, had previously been targeted in 2022 and the following year. The attack occurred days before Putin was due to meet the leaders of China and the United States.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the Crimean Bridge on Tuesday.
events.summary: Ukrainian drones and missiles destroyed the central road section of the bridge linking Russia and Crimea on Tuesday, using missiles from a Dutch-based company, prompting the Russian Embassy in the Netherlands to question Dutch involvement in the conflict.

events.extended_summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen for a first-ever trilateral meeting between the three nuclear-armed powers. Xi greeted Trump at the airport, the first time he had done so with any visiting leader since becoming president, and the two briefly hugged before walking to their motorcades. Xi pledged to stand up against trade protectionism while Putin criticized Western sanctions. The three leaders are scheduled to meet Thursday for one hour on the sidelines to discuss Russia's war with Ukraine, the US war in Iran, trade, AI and nuclear weapons. The choice of Shenzhen, home to tech giants Huawei, DJI and BYD and a record $1 trillion trade surplus this year, showcased China's high-tech rise amid US tech competition.
events.micro_summary: Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to hold first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen.
events.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping hosted US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin at the APEC summit in Shenzhen for a first-ever trilateral meeting, with Xi greeting Trump at the airport and pledging to oppose trade protectionism.

events.extended_summary: The US National Security Agency's highly classified internal communications network, NSANet, went offline on Tuesday during scheduled routine maintenance. The outage prompted the agency to close its campus to most employees, reverting to essential personnel only as it worked to restore the network. Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton attributed the disruption to software patching addressing major PHP vulnerabilities discovered last month, explaining that some systems did not come back up as expected after patching. An agency spokesperson stated that while some internal systems were affected, mission-critical capabilities remained fully operational and the ability to defend national security continued. There was no evidence the outage was caused by a cyberattack. The disruption followed a separate cyber incident on Tuesday in which malicious JavaScript was served to 178 websites, including major organizations, via a compromised third-party optimization platform.
events.micro_summary: NSA's classified communications network NSANet went offline during scheduled maintenance, with no evidence of cyberattack.
events.summary: The US National Security Agency's secure internal communications network, NSANet, experienced an outage during scheduled routine maintenance to patch PHP vulnerabilities. The agency closed its campus to most employees, but mission-critical capabilities remained operational with no evidence of a cyberattack.

events.extended_summary: Democratic lawmakers are demanding answers from US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding his handling of Nvidia while his former firm, Cantor Fitzgerald, held a significant stake in the tech company. Representatives Jamie Raskin, Gregory Meeks, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove sent a letter to Lutnick's son Brandon, who chairs Cantor Fitzgerald, requesting documents and communications concerning Nvidia. The lawmakers seek to determine whether Lutnick's decisions on export controls, enforcement measures, or national security policies were improperly influenced by the firm's holdings. At the time of Lutnick's confirmation in February 2025, Cantor Fitzgerald reportedly held more than 3.5 million Nvidia shares valued at over $1.3 billion. Lutnick, who led the firm for decades, transferred his stake to trusts benefiting his adult children upon joining the administration. The lawmakers specifically questioned whether Lutnick blocked efforts to stop suspected smuggling of advanced Nvidia chips to China while the firm held hundreds of millions of dollars in Nvidia stock. Cantor Fitzgerald maintains it had no role in the administration's decisions about Nvidia.
events.micro_summary: Democratic lawmakers demand answers from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick over his family firm's $1.3 billion Nvidia stake.
events.summary: Democratic lawmakers demanded documents from Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick regarding Cantor Fitzgerald's holdings of over 3.5 million Nvidia shares valued at more than $1.3 billion, questioning whether he compromised national security to benefit his adult children and the firm.

events.extended_summary: World Rugby has suspended South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus for six international matches with immediate effect following a review of comments he made about match officials. The governing body announced the sanction after an independent panel determined that Erasmus's remarks at a media conference in Dublin concerning the television match official's decisions during the Nations Championship match against France met the threshold for serious misconduct. The panel found the comments suggested officials acted with bias or deliberately influenced the match outcome. As a result, Erasmus will not be present at the Aviva Stadium for Saturday's match against Ireland and will instead host an online watchalong from his team's Dublin hotel. The suspension was imposed under the Match Official Abuse Sanction Process. Despite the ban, Erasmus retains support from former South African players who defended his right to question officiating.
events.micro_summary: World Rugby suspends Rassie Erasmus for six matches over comments on match officials.
events.summary: World Rugby has suspended South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus for six matches with immediate effect over comments about the television match official during the Nations Championship match against France. He will miss Saturday's game against Ireland at the Aviva Stadium.

events.extended_summary: Cameron Bancroft has alleged that all Australia players and coaches present in Cape Town during the 2018 Test against South Africa knew of the ball-tampering plot. In a detailed account, Bancroft supports claims by Usman Khawaja, who stated in his autobiography that "it was all of us" and that the team knew what was going on. Khawaja, who played 88 Tests for Australia, said they did it as a team. David Warner, the vice-captain who developed the plan and instructed Bancroft, along with captain Steve Smith and Bancroft, were the three players punished. Warner later played 133 more times for Australia, including the 2023 World Cup win, before retiring in 2024. Australia captain Pat Cummins denied Khawaja's version during a 68-minute news conference broadcast live on television.
events.micro_summary: Cameron Bancroft alleges all Australia players knew of 2018 sandpaper ball-tampering plot in South Africa.

sources.publisher: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

events.summary: Cameron Bancroft claims all Australia players and coaches knew of the 2018 ball-tampering plot in Cape Town, supporting Usman Khawaja's assertion that the whole team was aware, while captain Pat Cummins denied this version of events.

events.extended_summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed as Manchester United head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract, replacing Michael Carrick and officially starting work on Wednesday. The Argentine completed his duties with the United States national team after their 2-0 victory over Haiti in Cincinnati, finishing with a 62.16% win ratio from 37 games in charge. During his tenure, he led the US to the 2025 Gold Cup final and the last 16 of the 2026 World Cup. Meanwhile, 22-year-old Argentine midfielder Nico Paz scored twice in his country's 7-0 rout of Costa Rica, strengthening his reputation as the heir to Lionel Messi. Paz, who has been linked with United, is expected to be a target in the January transfer window, though Real Madrid hold an €80 million option to re-sign him in 2027. Pochettino's arrival is expected to boost United's bid to sign his fellow Argentine.
events.micro_summary: Mauricio Pochettino appointed Manchester United head coach on a two-and-a-half-year contract.
events.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has been appointed Manchester United head coach on a two-and-a-half-year deal, replacing Michael Carrick after finishing his US national team duties with a 2-0 win over Haiti.

events.extended_summary: Former UFC light heavyweight champion Jiri Prochazka headlines UFC Qatar in Doha against Navajo Stirling in the main event. Prochazka seeks to rebound from a knockout loss to Carlos Ulberg at UFC 327, where he admitted taking his foot off the gas after Ulberg suffered a torn ACL. The Czech fighter has worked on his psychological preparation to remain fully focused in the cage. Stirling, a teammate of Ulberg, has risen rapidly since his debut less than two years ago, recently destroying former champion Jan Blachowicz in under a round at UFC London. The card also features Ikram Aliskerov against Jared Cannonier, Kyoji Horiguchi against Asu Almabayev, and Dan Hooker against Brian Ortega. Prochazka believes a victory over Stirling would make him undeniable for another championship opportunity.
events.micro_summary: Jiri Prochazka faces Navajo Stirling in the main event of UFC Qatar in Doha.
events.summary: Former UFC light heavyweight champion Jiri Prochazka headlines UFC Qatar in Doha against Navajo Stirling, seeking to rebound from a knockout loss to Carlos Ulberg and position himself for another title shot.

events.extended_summary: On Tuesday, November 17, a Ryanair aircraft at Tenerife South Airport in the Canary Islands was evacuated following reports of a bomb threat. Spanish Civil Guard officers attended the airport, moved the plane to a safe area, and conducted a thorough search of the aircraft and luggage for explosives. The warning was subsequently declared a false alarm, and passengers were allowed to reboard after the all-clear was given. The flight's destination remains unclear, and there is no confirmed information regarding significant delays caused by the incident. The event occurred amid a series of similar security scares affecting passenger flights across Europe, though no connection between the cases has been confirmed. This was not the first such incident at the airport; in September, a Jet2 flight bound for London Stansted was evacuated after a passenger allegedly claimed to have a bomb, resulting in a delay of more than two hours.
events.micro_summary: On November 17, a Ryanair plane at Tenerife South Airport was evacuated after a bomb threat proved false.
events.summary: A Ryanair aircraft at Tenerife South Airport was evacuated on November 17 following a bomb threat. Spanish Civil Guard officers searched the plane and luggage, declared it a false alarm, and passengers reboarded. The flight's destination remains unclear.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian drones targeted one of Russia’s largest oil refineries in the republic of Bashkortostan as part of another record-setting overnight drone attack on Russian regions, officials and media reported Tuesday. Bashkortostan’s emergency situations committee claimed the Defense Ministry, security guards and mobile air defense groups had successfully repelled more than 50 Ukrainian drones. “All factories are operating as normal and there’s no critical damage,” it wrote on Telegram. The exiled outlet Astra analyzed eyewitness footage showing multiple fires and black smoke in the morning sky to identify the targeted facility as the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat refinery some 1,200 kilometers (746 miles) from the border with Ukraine. Ukraine's General Staff confirmed later Tuesday that it had struck the Salavat oil refinery. "Salavat is no ordinary plant. It is one of Russia's largest oil refining and petrochemical complexes, capable of processing about 10 million tons of oil a year," it said. Founded

events.extended_summary: The UK announced on 17 November a £240 million air defence support package for Ukraine to help defend against Russian attacks this winter. The package, part of a £500 million commitment announced at the Budget, includes more than 1,000 short-range air defence missiles and launchers proven effective against jet-powered drones, plus over a dozen air defence radars. Deliveries begin mid-December, building on 400 missiles already supplied. The announcement was made while co-chairing the 50-nation Ukraine Defence Contact Group at NATO Headquarters in Brussels. The US undersecretary of defence praised European efforts to support Ukraine, noting that in October Ukraine gained more territory than Russia for the second consecutive month while Russian forces suffered their highest monthly casualty toll of the war. He emphasized focusing support on frontline defence rather than deep strikes targeting civilian infrastructure.
events.micro_summary: The UK announced a £240 million air defence package for Ukraine including over 1,000 missiles.
events.summary: The UK announced a £240 million air defence package for Ukraine, including over 1,000 short-range missiles and a dozen radars, to counter Russian drone attacks this winter, with deliveries starting mid-December.

events.extended_summary: India's music industry generated ₹17,401 crore in value in 2025, up 45% from ₹12,047 crore in 2023. Digital platforms accounted for 52% of this value, followed by broadcasting at 21%, concerts at 16%, and filmed entertainment at 11%. Growth was driven by 233 million streamers consuming 16.4 billion streams daily, though 97% remained free or ad-supported, while paid subscribers rose to 14.4 million. Independent non-film music grew to 43% of digital consumption from 35% in 2023, with half of Spotify's top 10 Indian songs from independent artists. Live performances expanded to 130 concert days with over 10,000 attendees, up from 70 the previous year, and 61% of authors ranked live shows among their top three revenue sources. The industry produces 22,000 to 27,000 original songs annually, while companies pursued partnerships including Universal Music Group's 30% stake in Excel Entertainment and Saregama's ₹325 crore investment for 28% of Bhansali Productions.
events.micro_summary: India's music industry value surged 45% to ₹17,401 crore in 2025 driven by streaming and concerts.
events.summary: India's music economy reached ₹17,401 crore in 2025, up 45% from 2023, with digital platforms contributing 52%, while independent music rose to 43% of consumption and live events expanded to 130 major concert days.

Yash is the only Indian actor to headline films in two different languages that have grossed Rs 50 crore or more across every single territory in India (KGF: Chapter 2 and Ramayana). Ramayana has become the second Bollywood film in history to cross Rs 300 crore gross from the South Indian markets combined, trailing only Dhurandhar 2. events.extended_summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Prince William and Princess Catherine in New Delhi on 18 November 2026. The meeting focused on strengthening the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership, guided by India-UK Vision 2035 and bolstered by the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement that entered into force in July 2026. Modi commended the Earthshot Prize for promoting innovative solutions to global environmental challenges and appreciated its recognition of Indian innovators at the awards held in Mumbai on 17 November 2026. They exchanged views on cooperation in defense, health, education, fin-tech and people-to-people ties. Modi also conveyed warm regards to King Charles III and Prime Minister Andy Burnham.
events.micro_summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Prince William and Princess Catherine in New Delhi to strengthen the India-UK strategic partnership.
events.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi met Prince William and Princess Catherine in New Delhi on 18 November 2026, discussing the India-UK Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and commending the Earthshot Prize for recognizing Indian environmental innovators.

events.extended_summary: Synopsis: Bengaluru-based startups have raised about US$85 billion since 2010, accounting for 47% of all venture funding raised by Indian startups. Of that, startups raised US$76.5 billion in the past 10 years. The number of the city's active, funded startups since 2010 numbered 3,810, nearly twice Mumbai's 1,982. Bengaluru is consolidating its position as India's AI capital, with the city commanding 36.3% of the country's native AI startup funding and hosting 71% of India's AI and deep-tech unicorns created since 2023. The figures were part of the Bengaluru Innovation Report 2026, Karnataka's IT and BT Minister Priyank Kharge released at the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit on Wednesday, 18 November. Terming the city a deep tech powerhouse, the report said that of the 1,556 deep tech startups founded in Bengaluru since 2010, 1,319 were active and funded, together raising US$3.77 billion; and 764 of the city’s 799 native
events.micro_summary: Bengaluru is India’s AI, start-up capital; city captures 47% of national venture funding.

events.extended_summary: India secured a 22-run victory against New Zealand in the fifth ODI at Mount Maunganui on November 15, clinching the series 3-1. Chasing 209, New Zealand were bowled out for 187 after Ishan Kishan and Axar Patel scored 46 runs each for India. However, the Indian team was fined 35 percent of their match fee for maintaining a slow over-rate, having been seven overs short of the target after time allowances. ICC Match Referee Ranjan Madugalle imposed the sanction under Article 2.22 of the ICC Code of Conduct, which penalises players five percent of their match fees per over short. Captain Shreyas Iyer pleaded guilty to the offence and accepted the proposed sanction without a formal hearing.
events.micro_summary: India were fined 35% of match fees for slow over-rate in 22-run fifth ODI win over New Zealand.
events.summary: India defeated New Zealand by 22 runs in the fifth ODI in Mount Maunganui to win the series 3-1, but were fined 35% of their match fee for being seven overs short of the required over-rate.

events.extended_summary: India commences a two-match Test series against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington on Thursday, seeking victories to climb the World Test Championship rankings. This marks India's first Test tour of New Zealand since 2020, when they lost the two-match series 0-2, and follows a 0-1 defeat in 2014. India's last series triumph in New Zealand came in 2009 under M. S. Dhoni, when they won 1-0 after 41 years. In that 2009 series, India won the first Test in Hamilton by 10 wickets with Sachin Tendulkar scoring 160 and Harbajan Singh taking seven wickets, while the remaining two Tests ended in draws. Since 2015, the teams have met 11 times with India winning four and losing six. New Zealand has enjoyed mixed home results since 2022, defeating West Indies, Sri Lanka and South Africa but losing to Australia and England.
events.micro_summary: India begins two-match Test series against New Zealand in Wellington seeking World Test Championship improvement.
events.summary: India begins a two-match Test series against New Zealand at Wellington's Basin Reserve on Thursday, aiming to win and improve World Test Championship rankings after losing previous series 0-2 in 2020 and 0-1 in 2014.

events.extended_summary: India defeated Pakistan 2-1 in the South Asian Football Federation Championship final at the National Stadium in Dhaka, Bangladesh, to claim a record-extending 10th title and third consecutive crown. Pakistan took the lead before halftime through Alamgir Ghazi, but defender Junaid Shah received a straight red card for a high tackle early in the second half. India equalized through Suhail Bhat in the 60th minute and scored the winner when Sandip Mandi headed in during the 88th minute. More than 10,000 spectators attended the match, with many Bangladeshi fans supporting Pakistan while others backed India following Pakistan's semifinal victory over the hosts. India had previously defeated Bhutan 2-1 in the semifinal. Union Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya congratulated the team on achieving a historic hat-trick of consecutive SAFF titles.
events.micro_summary: India defeated Pakistan 2-1 to win their record 10th SAFF Championship title in Dhaka.
events.summary: India beat Pakistan 2-1 in the SAFF Championship final at Dhaka's National Stadium, securing their 10th title and third consecutive crown. Suhail Bhat and Sandip Mandi scored for India after Alamgir Ghazi gave Pakistan the lead.

He urged the court to adjourn the matter by two to three weeks, saying investigators had to follow international protocols.“There is no reason why we should delay deliberately,” Mehta said.The court agreed to take up the matter after two weeks. events.extended_summary: Pintu Mondal, a 46-year-old light boy working with Kolkata-based agency Light & Light, died on Tuesday morning after sustaining severe head injuries in a truck accident in Sikkim. The accident occurred on Monday around 3:30 pm near the 5th Mile on Jawaharlal Nehru Road when the truck carrying shooting equipment lost control while negotiating a sharp turn. Mondal was part of the technical crew for Maddock Films' production 'Mission Mirchi', which was being shot in Sikkim from November 15 to 20. The film crew was returning from Tsomgo Lake when the accident happened. Mondal was seated beside the driver, who also suffered critical shoulder injuries and is undergoing treatment at STNM Hospital, where Mondal was taken and later died.
events.micro_summary: A 46-year-old film technician died after a truck accident in Sikkim on Monday.
events.summary: Pintu Mondal, a 46-year-old film technician, died Tuesday after a truck carrying equipment crashed in Sikkim Monday; the driver suffered critical injuries.
